newsitem.title: PERU: Peru expects all hostages freed unharmed in siege.
newsitem.headline: Peru expects all hostages freed unharmed in siege.

text.p: Peruvian Prime Minister Alberto Pandolfi said on Monday he expected the siege at the Japanese ambassador's residence would end with the safe release of all 83 remaining hostages held by Marxist rebels.

"We are sure that the continuing sound handling of the situation will allow a solution that protects the physical well-being and lives of all of the hostages," the head of the government's cabinet said in a speech.

The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels have released more than 420 hostages, but still held top Peruvian officials, foreign diplomats and Japanese businessmen on the 13th day of the crisis.
There have been no releases since 20 hostages were freed on Saturday after the first face-to-face meeting between the rebels and the government.
"The government is working permanently with prudence and dedication for the prompt release" of the hostages, Pandolfi said.

After Saturday's release, the rebels appeared to soften their position, issuing the first statement since they stormed the residence that made no reference to their demand for the freeing of jailed comrades.

Publicly, the government has given no ground to the guerrillas. In his one address to the nation during the crisis, President Alberto Fujimori flatly rejected the rebels' demands and told them to release all the hostages and lay down their arms.
